key_insight: Augmenting street-view imagery with synchronized human gaze and individual perception labels reveals the perceptual process behind subjective urban judgments and lets models predict those judgments more accurately and interpretably.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between image-only urban perception models and the human perceptual process by providing gaze-grounded data and learning methods that connect where people look to how they evaluate urban scenes.
method: Collected Place Pulse-Gaze: a street-view dataset pairing images with synchronized eye-tracking recordings and individual subjective perception labels.
Trained gaze-informed models (multi-task / attention-guided) to jointly learn gaze patterns and perceptual judgments, using gaze as an auxiliary supervision signal.
Used gaze-based saliency and interpretability analyses to link visual cues (e.g., façades, greenery, clutter) with subjective scores and improve model explanations.
impact: Provides a human-centered supervisory signal that increases predictive performance and interpretability for subjective visual tasks; useful for building safer, fairer, and more explainable urban-scene models and transferring gaze supervision to other subjective AI problems.

paper_title: Modeling Subjective Urban Perception with Human Gaze
paper_authors: Lin Che, Xi Wang, Marc Pollefeys, Konrad Schindler, Martin Raubal
